doc.title: Vi Redd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999

title: Losing her son and brother; faith and church
summary: Redd speaks of her mother's death, her son's death in 1996, her brother's recent death, therapy, prayer and her church.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: I’m not going to use it anymore.

I can say this, when I retired from teaching school you know I taught a long time, and my family’s just — my mother went ‘92, then I went to Europe in ’94, and I said well I’m out of school now I can get back to really performing. Then my son was taken sick and he passed in ’96. And oh God, that was — I won’t even talk about it too much. And there was some malpractice involved and that made it even worse. He had a perforated intestine and they just messed all over it, so it made it very difficult for me. I was in therapy for eleven months, and doing pretty good. And last month my brother went. But I must understand that we don’t come to stay here forever. I had my mother and dad a long time. Mother was in her 80s and daddy was in his mid-70s. But the loss of a child at 36, he was my drummer, see, did business for me, had a little property that he managed, and it was just mind blowing. So Al got me to my therapy classes and I did a lot of praying.
My minister prayed with me much, and there were times when I thought I couldn’t make it.
Well the church is a big part of your life, isn’t it?

Yes it is. If it wasn’t, I don’t think I’d be here to talk about it. Yeah my church is important. I’m a member of Faith United Methodist Church. But I tell everybody I’m very ecumenical. I’m not hung up on people’s denominations. Tomorrow I may attend O.C.’s church, O.C. Smith? He has a Religious Science church, and I have a friend here from Chicago and she wanted to see his new edifice. So I may go there tomorrow.
